packageRules.description: Do not manage the legacy/ directory
Do not pin digests for Docker image tags referenced in Helm charts

Make `oci://` subcharts visible to Renovate. helmv3 extracts them with the `docker` datasource, and docker versioning cannot parse a semver range, so every OCI dependency was silently dropped as `unsupported/unversioned value ^x.y.z (versioning=docker)` while the https:// charts (helm datasource) updated normally. `helm` versioning understands the ranges. Charts sourced over https:// are unaffected — this rule only matches the docker datasource.

A Chart.yaml `version:` cannot carry an image digest, but the `docker:pinDigests` preset matches on datasource alone and would try to append one to the OCI subchart entries now that they resolve. The existing helm-values rule above does not cover them (different manager). This matters more now that the subchart versions are exact rather than ranges: a bare `31.0.0` is exactly the shape the preset would try to pin.

Subchart versions in Chart.yaml are exact, not ranges, so that Chart.lock is a function of Chart.yaml alone — see the pinning note in charts/materialize-monitoring/Chart.yaml. `pin` keeps them that way and re-pins anything that reintroduces a range. Renovate moves Chart.yaml only; the `auto-format` label on these PRs is what refreshes Chart.lock and the LFS-tracked archives under charts/*/charts/ (`make helm-deps`), which Renovate cannot do because it would push LFS pointers with no objects behind them.

Kubernetes puts its breaking changes in the minor, so for anything pinned to a k8s version v1.34 -> v1.36 is the risky bump and v1.34.8 -> v1.34.9 is the routine one. PVP versioning treats X.Y as the major version.
Treat Kubernetes major versions (X.Y+1 PVP versioning) as requiring manual review before opening.
Do not upgrade grafana-foundation-sdk to v10+. Only 0.0.x versions are valid

bin/fetch-grafana-schemas.sh pins a grafana-foundation-sdk git tag, which is a different dep from the pypi package above. That repo tags three families off one namespace -- the `v0.0.x` releases we want, a parallel `go/v0.0.x` set for the Go module, and `dashboard-converter-v1.0.0` -- and semver-coerced reads that last one as a 1.0.0 major bump. Capping the range keeps only the real releases in play; drop the cap if upstream ever leaves 0.0.x.
helm-docs is pinned to a commit pseudo-version; do not flag it as abandoned

Hugo is pinned twice: as a `tool` in go.mod, which is what the Makefile builds with `go run -tags extended`, and as `hugo-version` in the docs workflow, which installs a prebuilt binary. Group them so both move in a single PR. A split bump lets CI and local builds render with different Hugo versions, and that divergence is what let a non-extended local build hide behind a stale resource cache until an upgrade invalidated it.

peaceiris/actions-hugo wants a bare `0.165.0`, but the GitHub releases are tagged `v0.165.0`. Strip the prefix so the workflow keeps the form the action accepts. Scoped to hugo so the `v`-prefixed annotations elsewhere (kind, alloy) are untouched.

customManagers.description: Update renovate-annotated versions in GitHub workflows. The key pattern allows digits and hyphens so this covers `with:` inputs (`hugo-version:`) as well as env vars (`KIND_VERSION:`) — an unhyphenated class silently skipped every action input, which reads as 'nothing to update' rather than as a broken manager.

Update renovate-annotated versions in the vendoring scripts under bin/. Same annotation convention as the Dockerfile and workflow managers, but the variable name is unconstrained: these pins are git refs (`FSDK_REF`), not `*_VERSION`/`*_TAG` values, so the Dockerfile manager's name suffix would never match. Renovate moves only the pin -- the `auto-format` label on these PRs is what re-runs the script so the vendored output lands in the same PR.

Update renovate-annotated image refs (tag plus optional digest) in the Makefile. The bundled customManagers:makefileVersions preset only matches a bare version in a *_VERSION variable, so it cannot maintain an image:tag@sha256 pair. Capturing currentDigest is what bumps both halves together — a tag-only bump would leave the digest pinning the old image and silently win.
